newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-GERMAN PROSECUTORS WANT SIX YEARS JAIL FOR GRAF.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GERMAN PROSECUTORS WANT SIX YEARS JAIL FOR GRAF.

text.p: German prosecutors asked a court on Tuesday to sentence the father of world women's tennis number one seed Steffi Graf to six years and nine months in jail for tax evasion.

Federal prosecutor Gabriele Schoepf told the Mannheim court in her closing remarks that Peter Graf, 58, had tried to evade 19.2 million marks ($12.19 million) in tax on the tennis star's earnings between 1989 und 1993.
Schoepf also asked the court in Mannheim, southwestern Germany, to send Graf's former tax adviser Joachim Eckardt to jail for four years and nine months.
Eckardt has been facing tax evasion charges alongside Peter Graf in the trial that started last September.
Schoepf contested Graf and Eckardt were guilty of five counts of simple tax evasion and one count of serious evasion.
Graf's defence is due to make its closing statement in the next few days.
The court must then decide on a verdict and, if the verdict is guilty, a sentence. The verdict is expected on January 24.
Steffi Graf herself remains under investigation in the affair but investigators have said suspicions against her are not as serious as those against her father.
She has said she knew little about her financial affairs, entrusting them to her father from the start of a career which has taken her to the number one spot in women's tennis.
